summary: GREENANO is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in green nanotechnology. You study at the University of Lorraine in France, then in Italy and at the Jožef Stefan International Postgraduate School in Slovenia, and finish with an internship. Full scholarships pay tuition, registration, health insurance and €1,400 a month. Applications close on 6 January 2027.
meta_title: GREENANO 2027: Erasmus Mundus Green Nanotechnology scholarship
meta_description: GREENANO pays tuition, insurance and €1,400 a month for a two-year nanotechnology master's in France, Italy and Slovenia. Apply by 6 January 2027.
covers: Full exemption from tuition and registration fees at every partner university.
€1,400 a month for up to 24 months.
Health insurance for the whole programme.
Partial grants waive fees and include insurance but pay no monthly allowance.
eligibility: Applicants from every country. Each cohort has up to 25 students.

A bachelor's degree of at least three years (180 ECTS) in physics, materials science, chemistry, engineering, nanoscience or a related field. Final-year students can apply if they graduate before the programme starts.
English at B2 to C2: IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 90, TOEIC 850, PTE Academic 60 or a Cambridge CAE or CPE, no more than two years old.
Applicants from countries where English is an official language by law, such as Ghana and Nigeria, are exempt from the test but must show their bachelor's was taught in English if shortlisted.
how_to_apply: Apply on the University of Lorraine's GREENANO application platform between 15 October 2026 and 6 January 2027.

Upload your passport, a recent photo, a CV in English, your school and bachelor's diplomas with transcripts, your English certificate, two recommendation letters and a one- to two-minute introduction video.
A motivation letter of up to 600 words, proof of achievements and evidence of entrepreneurship are optional.
Shortlisted applicants are interviewed, and the committee then informs them of its decision.
watch_out: The maximum number of full scholarships for Pakistan and Bangladesh has already been reached for this intake.
Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 12 months after arrival in France.
Self-funded students pay their own travel, lodging and administrative costs.
costs: Waived for full and partial grant holders
€1,400 a month for full grant holders
documents: Photo taken within the last 12 months
High school and bachelor's diplomas with transcripts
English certificate or proof of exemption
A one- to two-minute introduction video

faq.a: Applications are open from 15 October 2026 to 6 January 2027.

faq.q: Do Ghanaian applicants need IELTS for GREENANO?
faq.a: No test is needed for applicants from countries where English is an official language by law, which includes Ghana and Nigeria. If shortlisted, you show that your bachelor's was taught in English and your English is checked at interview.

faq.q: What does a partial grant cover?
faq.a: Tuition, registration and health insurance, but no monthly allowance.
